intro: Buying a home in Wyoming requires more than finding a property with an affordable purchase price. Property taxes, mortgage interest, homeowners insurance and seasonal maintenance expenses can significantly influence your monthly housing budget.

Our free Wyoming mortgage calculator helps you estimate your monthly housing payment before purchasing a property. Whether you're buying in Cheyenne, Casper, Laramie, Sheridan or a smaller Wyoming community, compare financing arrangements and understand the complete cost of homeownership.

sections.heading: Quick Answer: How Much Is a Mortgage Payment in Wyoming?

blocks.markdown:
A $310,000 Wyoming home purchased with a 20% down payment and financed through a 30-year mortgage at a 6% fixed annual interest rate would have a monthly principal and interest payment of approximately $1,486.89.

Including illustrative property taxes and insurance produces the following estimate.
This example assumes no private mortgage insurance or association fees. Taxes, insurance premiums and the interest rate are illustrative planning assumptions rather than current statewide averages.

According to the [US Census Bureau's Wyoming housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/WY/LND110220), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $309,700 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among homeowners with mortgages were $1,754, while the homeownership rate was 71.8%.

These historical figures include homeowners who purchased properties under different market conditions. They do not represent current home sale prices or mortgage offers.

Housing prices around Jackson and popular mountain communities may differ considerably from those in eastern Wyoming or smaller agricultural communities.

Buyers considering rural properties should investigate transportation expenses, utility availability, insurance and infrastructure maintenance.

Research recent comparable property sales before establishing your purchase budget.

sections.heading: How to Use the Wyoming Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Start by entering your expected home purchase price and the amount you intend to contribute as a down payment.

Choose your preferred repayment period and enter the annual mortgage interest rate quoted by your lender.

If you have not received a quote, consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national benchmark.

Next, enter annual property taxes, homeowners insurance premiums and applicable association fees.

Include private mortgage insurance if required by your conventional financing arrangement.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and adjust individual inputs to compare borrowing scenarios.

The amortization schedule shows how your outstanding mortgage balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing arrangements outside Wyoming.

sections.heading: How Wyoming Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
Wyoming calculates property taxes using property valuations, statutory assessment percentages, applicable local mill levies and eligible exemptions.

County assessors establish property values, while local taxing districts determine rates that support public schools, emergency services and other government functions.

### Wyoming residential property assessment ratio

According to the [Wyoming Department of Revenue's residential property tax guidance](https://wyo-prop-div.wyo.gov/residential), residential property is generally assessed at 9.5% of its applicable market value.

For example, a residential property valued at $310,000 would have an assessed value of $29,450 before applicable exemptions.

The assessment ratio determines the value used for taxation. It does not mean homeowners pay 9.5% of their property's market value in annual property taxes.

Local mill levies are applied to the resulting taxable amount.

Wyoming provides a property tax exemption covering 25% of the first $1 million of qualifying residential market value.

Beginning in 2026, the exemption requires qualifying owner occupancy and an application.

According to [Albany County's homeowner exemption guidance](https://www.albanycountywy.gov/1594/Property-Tax-Exemption-for-Homeowners), homeowners generally must occupy the property as their primary residence for at least eight months during the applicable year.

Applications open on October 1 and generally must be submitted by March 1 for the relevant tax year. Homeowners must renew their applications annually.

Certain additional eligibility requirements and statutory exceptions apply.

### Wyoming property tax calculation example

Suppose your home has a fair market value of $310,000 and qualifies for the 25% homeowner exemption.

Assume a hypothetical combined property tax levy of 80 mills.

Without the exemption, the same hypothetical property would have annual taxes of $2,356.

The exemption would therefore reduce annual taxes by $589 under these assumptions.

Actual tax liabilities depend on property classification, applicable levies and confirmed exemption eligibility.

### Long-term homeowner tax relief

Wyoming also provides a separate property tax exemption for qualifying older homeowners with a substantial history of paying residential property taxes in the state.

Under [House Bill 45, enacted in 2026](https://wyoleg.gov/Legislation/2026/HB0045), eligibility generally requires the homeowner or spouse to be at least 65 years old and to have paid Wyoming residential property taxes for at least 25 years.

Primary residence and application requirements also apply.

Homeowners should not combine the ordinary homeowner exemption with the long-term homeowner exemption when the programs prohibit overlapping benefits.

Insurance premiums depend on your property's location, construction, replacement cost, condition and environmental exposure.

Wyoming homeowners may experience wildfires, severe winds, hailstorms, heavy snowfall and freezing temperatures.

Obtain written insurance quotes before completing your purchase.

### Wildfire insurance

Properties near forests, grasslands and mountainous communities may face additional wildfire exposure.

Ask insurers whether the property's location affects coverage availability, premiums or required protective measures.

Investigate roofing materials, surrounding vegetation and emergency access.

A relatively affordable property may become more expensive to own if suitable insurance coverage is difficult to obtain.

### Wind, hail and winter weather

Review whether your homeowners insurance policy includes separate wind or hail deductibles.

Ask insurers how they settle roof damage claims and whether coverage reflects replacement cost or depreciated value.

For example, a hypothetical 2% deductible on $300,000 in dwelling coverage would represent $6,000 in potential out-of-pocket expenses for an applicable covered claim.

### Flood insurance

Standard homeowners insurance generally excludes flooding.

Properties near rivers, streams and areas exposed to snowmelt runoff may require additional protection.

Use the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home) to investigate potential flood exposure.

Include applicable additional insurance premiums in your mortgage estimate without counting overlapping coverage twice.
The following estimates assume a 20% down payment, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.

These estimates exclude property taxes, homeowners insurance, PMI and association fees.

Compare complete monthly housing expenses rather than relying exclusively on principal and interest.

The Wyoming Community Development Authority, commonly known as WCDA, offers mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### First-Time Homebuyer Program

The [WCDA homebuyer programs](https://www.wyomingcda.com/homebuyers/) include fixed-rate mortgage financing for eligible first-time purchasers.

Applicants must satisfy applicable income, purchase price, property and underwriting requirements.

### Home$tretch down payment assistance

The Home$tretch program provides qualifying borrowers with up to $15,000 toward eligible purchase expenses.

The assistance carries a 0% interest rate and requires no scheduled monthly payments.

Repayment becomes due when the property is sold, the mortgage is refinanced or the secondary loan reaches its 30-year maturity.

Published requirements generally include a minimum credit score of 620 and a minimum borrower contribution of $1,500, which may come from an eligible gift.

Home$tretch is deferred financing rather than an unconditional grant.

### Amortizing down payment assistance

WCDA also offers an amortizing assistance loan through its Advantage mortgage product.

Qualifying borrowers may receive up to $15,000, repayable through scheduled monthly payments over a maximum ten-year term.

Unlike Home$tretch, this option increases recurring borrowing expenses.

Request the applicable interest rate and repayment schedule before incorporating assistance into your budget.

### Spruce Up financing

WCDA's Spruce Up program combines eligible home purchase and rehabilitation expenses into one financing arrangement.

This may be useful when purchasing an older Wyoming property requiring roofing, plumbing, heating or accessibility improvements.

Confirm that your proposed improvements and property meet program requirements.

sections.heading: Additional Costs of Owning a Wyoming Home

blocks.markdown:
Wyoming homeowners should prepare for winter heating, snow removal, transportation and ongoing property maintenance.

Rural properties may also involve private wells, septic systems and access road repairs.

Properties containing substantial acreage or agricultural operations may require specialized financing instead of an ordinary residential mortgage.

Request historical utility bills and investigate maintenance obligations before purchasing.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in Wyoming?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Use our [Wyoming Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/wyoming-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate after-tax earnings and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate outstanding borrowing commitments.

Wyoming does not impose an individual state income tax, although federal taxes and applicable payroll deductions still reduce available earnings.

Compare mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Maintain sufficient emergency savings for closing expenses, insurance deductibles and unexpected repairs.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $310,000 Wyoming home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $1,486.89. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total payment.

### What is Wyoming's 25% homeowner property tax exemption?

Qualifying homeowners may receive an exemption covering 25% of the first $1 million of eligible residential market value. Primary residence, occupancy and annual application requirements apply.

### Does Wyoming offer $15,000 in down payment assistance?

Yes. WCDA offers eligible borrowers up to $15,000 through its Home$tretch and amortizing assistance programs. Repayment obligations and eligibility requirements depend on the selected financing arrangement.

Use our Wyoming mortgage calculator to compare purchase prices, down payments, interest rates and repayment periods.
